judgments.reasoning_cat1: The execution date is illegible ("July ¥, 2005"), so the "Effective Date" — the trigger for the Employment Term, the commission period and the Reorganization Bonus — cannot be fixed from the text itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble says "The Company" (both Ajuba and Ajuba India) employs the Employee, while Section 2.1 says Ajuba India employs him and all pay obligations in 2.2 fall on Ajuba India, leaving the identity of the employer contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line definition tying "Board" to Ajuba's directors; no term in it bears two meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1 has Employee reporting to "the Board (or selected designee of the Board of Directors of the Parent)" while Schedule 2.1 says he reports to the Chairman, a mild strain on the defined term but not a squarely inconsistent one.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Business" ends with the open catch-alls "such other entities serviced by the Company" and "other related services" after a long enumerated list, a classic ejusdem generis/general-vs-specific problem, and it is the operative reach of the Article V noncompete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts directly with Section 1.6 ("Core Business") and Article V(a)/(d), and the width of "Business" versus the narrower Core Business substitution is exactly where the parties' readings would diverge.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard statutory definition with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Code" is defined but never used anywhere else in the instrument — surplusage, not an inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "known to the Employee as a consequence of or through the Employee's employment" is a vague boundary, and the definition covers pre-existing knowledge as readily as created work.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.1 requires assignment of inventions "relating in any way to the Business" that Employee "conceived, developed or acquired," a scope broader than this definition, creating a fit problem between the definition and the operative assignment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "all information, in whatever form, regarding Parent, the Company their Business and their clients" is boundless and has a missing comma, with an illustrative rather than limiting list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.1's carve-outs (public domain, rightful receipt, legal compulsion) cabin it, so the pieces broadly cohere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (b)(ii) is mathematically circular — first-year revenue must exceed the sum of 1% of consolidated revenue plus that same first-year revenue — and the "either (i) ... or (ii)" structure sits awkwardly against limb (a), so the definition's reach is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the substitute term imported by Article V(d) on a Section 8.4 termination, so the defect propagates into the enforceability of the post-8.4 noncompete.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "actively sought" and "material contact" are soft boundaries, and the clause measures from "the date of termination of this Agreement" rather than termination of employment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Agreement elsewhere speaks of termination of employment (Article VIII, Sections 3.2, 4.2), so the trigger date in this definition does not align cleanly with the termination machinery.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is formulaic, though it shifts between lowercase "fiscal year" and the defined "Fiscal Year" and makes Ajuba's own accountants the arbiter.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds Sections 2.2(a) and 2.2(b) bonus thresholds; the accountant-resolution sentence could be read against the venue clause 9.15, but no direct contradiction appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "third anniversary of this Agreement" is a slightly different referent from the Effective Date, but on these facts the two coincide.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.1 measures from "the third anniversary of the Effective Date" and Section 1.15 builds the Restricted Period on the end of the Employment Term; the mismatch is small but real.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ordinary calendar-year definition with a standard change mechanism.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the bonus tables in 2.2(b) and with the EBITDA definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A named-entity definition with nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parent's role is picked up consistently in 1.5, 1.7 and 9.9 (third-party beneficiary).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "other entity" is a catch-all inside a short list, but the definition is deliberately inclusive and harmless.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only in Section 2.1(b); no tension elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Geographic definition that is definite on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the "United States and India" scope in the Business definition and Article V(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The period runs from the date of the Agreement to three years after the end of the Employment Term, producing a restraint of up to six years — extreme duration is a construction and enforceability flashpoint even though the words are arithmetically clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Article V(e)'s acknowledgment that the restraints are "reasonable in ... duration," the Article VII blue-pencil sentence, and the separate Non-Competition Agreement preserved by Section 9.8.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The duties are defined by open-ended standards ("customarily performed by a President," "such other legally permissible and proper duties ... consistent with Employee's position") and the full-time devotion covenant carries three loosely bounded carve-outs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says Employee reports to the Board while Schedule 2.1 says he reports to the Chairman, and it deems Schedule 2.1 amended by the 8.4(a) consolidation/outsourcing carve-out — a live tension with the Good Reason definition in 8.4(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The EBITDA step-up is ambiguous as to which year's EBITDA counts and what "retroactive to the first business day of the year following" means, and "Base Salary" is set at $270,000 for each remaining fiscal year with an increase that may or may not persist.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Allowance is paid "in lieu of receiving health, dental and other benefits afforded to Ajuba US employees," which sits uneasily with Section 2.2(c)'s entitlement to participate in all benefit plans made available to senior executives.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "eligible to receive" against a fixed threshold table is ambiguous as to entitlement, and the final sentence about the 2007 Bonus is garbled ("unless such employee is terminated pursuant to Sections 8.3 or 8.4 after December 31, 2007").
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 8.2, 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5 each state different rules about bonuses for "the prior or current year," and 8.2/8.5's blanket denial of any bonus is hard to square with the earned-bonus sentence here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An entitlement to participate in "all" plans coupled with an unqualified right to modify or discontinue them at "sole discretion" is internally self-undercutting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.2(a) gives the Allowance expressly in lieu of health and other benefits, and Sections 8.2–8.5 cut off benefit participation on termination; the interaction with this clause is genuinely uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "substantially similar to the D&O Policy maintained by the Company immediately prior to the date hereof" is a soft benchmark, but it is a familiar and workable one.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Samii" is never defined, "net sales" is undefined, and the trigger "goes live" appears in quotation marks without definition; the two commission rates also turn on undefined conditions about the Company's sales force.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 8.3 and 8.4 cross-refer to "Section 2.2(e)" for the Reorganization Bonus, which is in fact 2.2(f) — this Commissions subsection — so the cross-references collide with this provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "when and if the Company's UK office is shut down and the Company's Novi office is restructured ... in accordance with Schedule I" leaves the earning event and its timing (versus payment on the twelve-month anniversary) open to two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 8.3 and 8.4 preserve the Reorganization Bonus "in accordance with Section 2.2(e)," a mis-citation of this subsection (2.2(f)), and Schedule I's completion definitions depend on third-party lease terminations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "reasonable out-of-pocket expenses" in accordance with Company policies is ordinary and administrable language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A breach here is Good Reason under 8.4(c), a coherent linkage; nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The covenant is perpetual and the exceptions are conventional and clearly drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article VII's reference to breaches of "Articles I, IV or V" appears to mean Article III; that mis-citation touches this provision's enforcement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain return-on-termination obligation with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates Exhibit A ¶2's broader return obligation, but the two run in the same direction.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit A ¶13 repeats the same formula, so the instrument is at least consistent about it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading is mis-numbered ("4." for 4.1) and the assignment reaches "all inventions, improvements, technical information and suggestions relating in any way to the Business," language broader than the term it purports to define as Company Technology.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear obligation to return and stop using Company Technology on termination.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 1.4 and 4.1 and with Exhibit A ¶¶2 and 5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "engage in any activity which is in competition with the Business" imports the open-ended Business definition and ends its list of capacities with "or otherwise," a general catch-all after enumerated specifics.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "directly or indirectly in competition with the Business" and "accept from any Customer any such competitive business" are broad but the conduct prohibited is identifiable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is a single sprawling construction with a lowercase "the company," and the Supervisor-and-above carve-out is drafted so that the advertising proviso is hard to reconcile with the sentence it qualifies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "the six months prior to termination of Employee's employment" measures from a different point than the Customer definition's termination-of-Agreement date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The substitution turns entirely on whether the termination was "pursuant to Section 8.4," and because 8.4 covers both company termination and employee resignation for Good Reason or "any other reason," the trigger is ambiguous on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.5 separately lets the Employee resign "for any reason," so whether a voluntary resignation is under 8.4 or 8.5 — and thus whether the narrower Core Business applies — cannot be resolved from these clauses read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A boilerplate acknowledgment of reasonableness; nothing operative to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against the up-to-six-year Restricted Period and Article VII's blue-pencil sentence, a mild but not squarely contradictory tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard three-limb representation, definite in its terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ordinary no-conflict representation with a conventional "without limitation" example.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the instrument cuts against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite termination-date rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (c) cites "Articles I, IV, V or VI" where Article III must be meant, limb (d) begins with a stray "or," and "conduct causing ... substantial public disgrace or disrepute" is an inherently vague Cause trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cure right is expressed as an opportunity "to cure such failure" although several Cause grounds (fraud, felony conviction) are not curable, and the bonus forfeiture sentence collides with the earned-bonus language in 2.2(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Disability" is defined with a quantified test, but "substantially failed to perform his essential duties ... with or without reasonable accommodation" leaves the standard soft.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The severance measure — "the compensation at the rate or level, as applicable, in effect on the date of such termination, through the third anniversary of the Effective Date" — does not say whether it captures Allowance, Bonus or commissions, and 8.4(a)'s diminution carve-out is drafted in a nearly unreadable double-negative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The second sentence lets Employee terminate "for any other reason pursuant to this Section 8.4," which cannot be reconciled with Section 8.5's separate no-severance resignation right, and it again mis-cites the Reorganization Bonus to Section 2.2(e).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "effective as of a date chosen by the Company, however, no later than thirty (30) business days" is awkward, and no minimum notice is specified, but the payment consequence is plain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard headings clause with nothing to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional notices clause; "deemed properly given when delivered" by fax or overnight service is workable though it lacks deemed-receipt timing for mail.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is definite, but the carve-out for "that certain Non-Competition Agreement of even date herewith" leaves the relationship between two simultaneous restrictive-covenant regimes unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article V of this Agreement is itself a full noncompete, so the preserved separate Non-Competition Agreement and Article V may impose overlapping or differing restraints — a genuine whole-instrument question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite; "the Parties" is not a capitalised defined term here, but its meaning is obvious.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parent (MiraMed) is given rights under 1.5, 1.7 and 8.4(b) though it is not a signatory, and this clause deliberately accommodates that.
